verses.hebrew: זֶה הַשִּׁיר הַמֻּבְחָר שֶׁל שְׁלֹמֹה.
verses.english: This is the songThat weaves together several of the songsAbout one beautiful country-girlWho was forcibly separated from her shepherd boy loverAnd taken to Shlomo.

verses.hebrew: נַשֵּׁק אוֹתִי מִנְּשִׁיקוֹת פִּיךָ, כִּי אַהֲבָתְךָ טוֹבָה יוֹתֵר מִיַּיִן.
verses.english: Song 1The country girl senses her former beloved standing outside the locked palace door. She speaks softly, as though to herself:If only we weren't separated by the palace wall —He could kiss meWith the passionate kisses of his mouth.She turns toward the door and addresses him:You realize,Your love is dearer to meThan the fine wines and luxuriesThat surround me in the palace.

verses.hebrew: שִׁמְךָ הַטּוֹב יוֹצֵא לְפָנֶיךְ כְּרֵיחַ שֶׁל שְׁמָנִים מְבֻשָּׂמִים וּבְסִבָּתָם נְעָרוֹת מִתְאַהֲבוֹת בְּךָ.
verses.english: Even the elite young women in this haremAre in love with you,Even though they have not seen you;Because of the scent of your fragrant oils,And your fine reputation that wafts like perfume oil.One can only imagine how mesmerised they would beShould they set their eyes on your beautyAnd behold your virtue firsthand.

verses.hebrew: מְשׁוֹךְ אוֹתִי אֵלֶיךָ וְנָרוּץ יַחַד אַחֲרֶיךָ כְּקֶדֶם, כְּשֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ הִכְנִיס אוֹתִי אֶל חֲדָרָיו, נָגִיל וְנִשְׂמַח בְּךָ, נִשְׁאַף מֵרֵיחַ אַהֲבָתְךָ הַטּוֹבָה יוֹתֵר מִיַּיִן, אוֹהֲבִים אוֹתְךָ בְּנֶאֱמָנוּת.
verses.english: Please draw me out of the palace —My lady friends will come too;We will all run after you!I am confined here, brought by the kingTo live with him in his chambers.We will delight in the rush of freedomAnd then permanently rejoice with you!We will continuously recall your love —More than the wine and royal luxury,Because we genuinely admire who you are!Palace luxuries offer fleeting self-indulgence;You offer lasting virtue and substance.

verses.hebrew: אֲנִי אֻמַּת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, גַּם כְּשֶׁאֵינֶנִּי מְאִירַת פָּנִים עֲדַיִן בְּתוֹכִי אֲנִי נָאָה, כְּמוֹ אוֹהָלִים מֻכֵּי שֶׁמֶשׁ כְּמוֹ יְרִיעוֹת בְּמִקְדַּשׁ שְׁלֹמֹה.
verses.english: She turns to her attendants:O' daughters of Jerusalem,Tasked with watching my every step to ensure I do not escape:Do not scorn me that I am dark skinned,For in essence I am fair.Just like the blackened tents of KedarIn essence identical to the whitest sheeting of Shlomo —They can regain their whiteness if thoroughly washed.My darkness is but a deep suntanFrom a life spent outdoors with my flocks;Should I remain indoors, my fairness will return.

verses.hebrew: אַל תִּסְתַּכְּלוּ עָלַי כָּכָה עַל שֶׁאֲנִי כֵּהָה, זֶה רַק שִׁזּוּף בַּשֶּׁמֶשׁ, בְּנֵי עַמִּי זִלְזְלוּ בִּי וְשָׁלְחוּ אוֹתִי לִשְׁמוֹר בְּכַרְמֵי זָרִים, לֹא בַּכֶּרֶם שֶׁלִּי.
verses.english: Do not surmise that you are beholding my true selfWhen you set eyes on my darkness,For I was greatly exposed to the sun.Besides my shepherding,My mother’s sons tasked me with watching the vines,Thus parching my flesh beneath the scorching sun.I could not tend to my personal vine —That is, my beautiful fair skin.

verses.hebrew: סַפֵּר לִי אָהוּב נַפְשִׁי, אֵיךְ אַתָּה רוֹעֶה אֶת צֹאנְךָ? כֵּיצַד אַתָּה גּוֹרֵם לוֹ לִרְבּוֹץ כְּחוֹם הַיּוֹם? לָמָּה שֶׁאֶהְיֶה כְּמוֹ אֲבֵלָה עַל עֶדְרֵי אֲהוּבֶיךָ שֶׁעָלַי לִרְעוֹת!
verses.english: She resumes her heart-to-heart with her beloved:Tell me, love of my soul:Where can I find you at pasture with the flocks?Where can I find you resting in the afternoon shade,Alongside the flocks of your fellow shepherds?Although my every step is watched,When I get the chance to escape I shall join you there!For, how can I —A free-spirited rural girl steeped in the outdoors —Be enshrouded in the gloomy confines of this urban palace?

verses.hebrew: – הַיָּפָה שֶׁבַּנָּשִׁים, אִם אֵינֵךְ יוֹדַעַת – צְאִי בְּעִקְבוֹת רוֹעֵי הַצֹּאן וּרְעִי אֶת הַגְּדִיּוֹת שֶׁלָּךְ עַל יַד מְקוֹם הָרוֹעִים הַבְּקִיאִים.
verses.english: The shepherd boy responds:O' fairest among the women,That is impossibleUnless you know my location —And this you can only findBy following in the footsteps of the sheep.But you must also escape detection:Throughout your journey to discover me,Disguise yourself as a shepherd girlAnd pasture your lambs near the shepherds' dwellings.

verses.hebrew: דּוֹמָה אַתְּ רַעֲיָתִי לְסוּסַת רְכִיבָה מִצְרִית זְרִיזָה.
verses.english: The country girl heeds his advice, and one day — still bedecked in her royal jewellery — she escapes the palace and reunites with her beloved.The shepherd boy, beholding her, says:My one and only soul-mate —It is as though my one and only horse was confiscatedTo pull Pharaoh's chariot along with all his other horses.Does not Shlomo have so many wives and concubines?Yet he fancied youAnd so deprived me of you,My one and only love.

verses.hebrew: לְחָיַיִךְ כֹּה נָאִים בַּתַּכְשִׁיטִים הַמְּשֻׁלָּשִׁים, וְצַוָּארֵךְ כֹּה יָפֶה בַּחֲרוּזִים.
verses.english: That said — look at your breathtaking appearance!How fair are your cheeks with their golden braids,O' royal horse;How grand is your neck with its strings of pearls.

verses.hebrew: נַעֲשֶׂה לָךְ מְשֻׁלְּשֵׁי זָהָב עִם נְקֻדּוֹת כֶּסֶף.
verses.english: The silver droplets —That you once owned as a simple country girl —Have been transformed for you into golden braids!

verses.hebrew: – בְּעוֹד שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ יוֹשֵׁב לִשְׁתּוֹת גַּם הַבּוֹשֶׂם שֶׁלִּי מַדִּיף רֵיחַ.
verses.english: The country girl replies:The fine scent of you,My spikenard-like beloved,Reached all the way to the king's banquet.I had no appetite —My mind was preoccupied with you.

verses.hebrew: אֲהוּבִי הוּא עֲבוּרִי כְּמוֹ חֲבִילַת בּוֹשֶׂם הַמּוֹר, הוּא יָבוֹא לִישׁוֹן בְּחֵקִי.
verses.english: You, my beloved, are engraved on my heart;I cannot stop thinking about you —Like the scent of the sachet of myrrhThat rests between my breasts,Its fragrance constantly arousing my senses.

verses.hebrew: אֲהוּבִי הוּא עֲבוּרִי כְּמוֹ אֶשְׁכּוֹל בּוֹשֶׂם הַכּוֹפֶר שֶׁגָּדֵל בְּעֵין גֶּדִי.
verses.english: You, my beloved, are like a vibrant cluster of hennaWhose fine scent wafts far and wide;I smell you in JerusalemAlthough you are so distant,In the vineyards of Ein Gedi.

verses.hebrew: אַתְּ יָפָה רַעֲיָתִי, עֵינַיִךְ יָפוֹת כְּמוֹ יוֹנִים.
verses.english: The shepherd boy says:You are so fairBecause you are my faithful soulmate.Yes, you are so inherently fair —Especially because your eyes are true to me,Unfailingly faithful like a dove.

verses.hebrew: – אַתָּה יָפֶה אֲהוּבִי וְגַם נָעִים, וְגַם מִטָּתֵנוּ רַעֲנָנָה.
verses.english: The country girl says:You too are so physically attractive, my love,Also so virtuous.How I desire to lie with you here beneath the trees —Look, the foliage that shall be our makeshift bed is lush.

verses.hebrew: תִּקְרַת בֵּיתֵנוּ מֵאֲרָזִים, וְהַנְּסָרִים הַמֻּחְלָקִים עֲשׂוּיִים מִבְּרוֹשִׁים.
verses.english: Let the forest cedars be the makeshift beams of our home;The broad branches of the forest cypressesThe plumbery protecting us from rain.

verses.hebrew: אֲנִי כְּמוֹ פֶּרַח חֲבַצֶּלֶת הַשָּׁרוֹן, כְּמוֹ שׁוֹשַׁנַּת הָעֵמֶק.
verses.english: I am like the Sharon tulip — beautiful and heliotropic,And the lily of the valleys — whose delectable scent peaks at dusk.In your shining company I unrestrainedly express my outward beauty;In the shadowy palace I instead exhale my virtue of character.

verses.hebrew: – כְּמוֹ שׁוֹשַׁנָּה בֵּין קוֹצִים כָּךְ רַעְיָתִי בֵּין הַבָּנוֹת.
verses.english: Her lover responds:Indeed, a tender but fragrant lilySurrounded by thornsIs the likeness of my soulmateIn the company of the court women.My outnumbered but outstanding —Distance yourself from themLest their barbs taint our pure love.

verses.hebrew: – כְּמוֹ עֵץ תַּפּוּחַ בֵּין עֲצֵי יַעַר כָּךְ אֲהוּבִי בֵּין הַבָּנִים, בְּצִלּוֹ חָמַדְתִּי לָשֶׁבֶת וּפִרְיוֹ מָתוֹק לְפִי.
verses.english: The country girl replies:My beloved too is like a fragrant and fruitful apple tree;Though dwarfed by the towering forest trees,He is the most attractive of them all.I desire his shade and so there I shall sit;How sweet are his fruits to my palate.

verses.hebrew: הוּא הֱבִיא אוֹתִי לְחֵדֶר הַיַּיִן וְהֵנִיף עָלַי אַהֲבָה.
verses.english: She narrates:He ushered me into the wine houseAnd spread his banner over me —He showered me with love.

verses.hebrew: שִׂימוּ בְּצִידִי גְּבִיעֵי יַיִן, רַפְּדוּ אֶת מְקוֹמִי בְּתַפּוּחִים, כִּי אֲנִי חוֹלַת אַהֲבָה.
verses.english: I called out:"Provide me with goblets of wine,Lay out for me a bed of fragrant apples,For I am lovesick."

verses.hebrew: יַד שְׂמֹאלוֹ תּוֹמֶכֶת בְּרֹאשִׁי בְּחִבָּה, וְיַד יְמִינוֹ מְחַבֶּקֶת אוֹתִי.
verses.english: He heeded my desireAnd made love with me;He placed his left hand under my head,Embraced me with his right arm.

verses.hebrew: מַשְׁבִּיעָה אֲנִי אֶתְכֶם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּצְּבָיִים אוֹ בָּאַיָּלוֹת שֶׁבַּשָּׂדֶה, אַל תָּעִירוּ וְאַל תְּעוֹרְרוּ אֶת הָאַהֲבָה עַד שֶׁתַּחְפּוֹץ לְהִתְעוֹרֵר מֵעַצְמָהּ.
verses.english: But the court women of Jerusalem were hot on her trail.She turns in their direction and exclaims:I bind you under oath,O daughters of Jerusalem —Let the gazelles and does be witness:Neither douse nor arouse our love!Let me be;Allow my desire to be realized.

verses.hebrew: אֲנִי שׁוֹמַעַת אֶת קוֹל בּוֹאוֹ שֶׁל אֲהוּבִי, הוּא מְדַלֵּג עַל הָרִים, מְקַפֵּץ מֵעַל גְּבָעוֹת.
verses.english: Song 2With her escapade over, the country girl is returned to the palace, where she endures the long autumnal and winter months, far from her beloved. Then spring arrives, and with it her beloved shepherd boy, intent on reigniting their love.The country girl speaks:Behold! The voice of my beloved —I detect it from afar!He is coming now,Leaping over the mountains,Skipping over the hills,Towards me.

verses.hebrew: אֲהוּבִי דּוֹמֶה לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעוֹפֶר בֶּן אַיָּלָה, הִנֵּה הוּא כְּבָר עוֹמֵד מֵאֲחוֹרֵי הַקִּיר, מַשְׁגִּיחַ עָלַי מִן הַחַלּוֹנוֹת, מֵצִיץ מִן הַחֲרַכִּים.
verses.english: My beloved resembles a gazelle or a young hartAs he gracefully bounds across the landscape.And here he is!I sense him standing on the far side of our wall —He observes me through the windows,Straining to break through the lattice!

verses.hebrew: עָנָה לִי אֲהוּבִי וְאָמַר: קוּמִי לָךְ רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּבוֹאִי!
verses.english: My beloved spoke up and said to me:Arise my beloved, o' my fair one —The time is ripe to escape from here.

verses.hebrew: כִּי הִנֵּה הַסְּתָיו עָבָר, הַגֶּשֶׁם חָלַף וְהָלַךְ לוֹ.
verses.english: For behold, the autumn has passed;The winter rains are over,Entirely gone.

verses.hebrew: בָּאָרֶץ כְּבָר נִרְאִים נִצָּנִים, עוֹנַת הַזָּמִיר הִגִּיעָה וְקוֹל הַיּוֹנִים נִשְׁמַע בְּאַרְצֵנוּ.
verses.english: The blossoms have appeared on the land,The time for bird-song has arrived;Even the chirp of the turtledove —Returned from its winter migration —Is heard in our land.

verses.hebrew: פַּגֵּי הַתְּאֵנָה חָנְטוּ וּסְמָדַר הַגְּפָנִים מַדִּיף רֵיחַ, קוּמִי לָךְ רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּבוֹאִי!
verses.english: The fig tree has produced its early green figs;The grapevines their tender grapesThat give out their delectable fragrance.Arise my soulmate, o' my fair one —The time is ripe to escape from here.The gloomy wintry past is behind us;A bright and vibrant future awaits.

verses.hebrew: אֲהוּבָתִי מִסְתַּתֶּרֶת בִּנְקִיקֵי הַסֶּלַע, מֵאֲחוֹרֵי הַמַּדְרֵגָה; הַרְאִי לִי אֶת מַרְאֵךְ, הַשְׁמִיעִי לִי אֶת קוֹלֵךְ, כִּי קוֹלֵךְ עָרֵב וּמַרְאֵךְ נָאֶה.
verses.english: My dove,Nesting in the clefts of the rock,Who dares not leave her confinesNor sound her songful voice,For she is in hiding,Concealed in the precipice —Show me your appearance,Sound for me your voice,For your voice is so pleasantAnd your appearance so fair.

verses.hebrew: תִּפְסוּ לָנוּ אֶת הַשּׁוּעָלִים הַקְּטַנִּים הַמְּחַבְּלִים בַּכְּרָמִים, כִּי בַּכֶּרֶם שֶׁלָּנוּ הָעֲנָבִים קְטַנְטַנִּים.
verses.english: One fine spring day, while strolling through the vineyards around Jerusalem, the country girl turns to her entourage:"Go and seize for us the foxes —Those pesky little foxes that damage vineyards —For our vines are laden with tender grapes."

verses.hebrew: אֲהוּבִי מְיוֹעָד לִי וַאֲנִי מְיוֹעֶדֶת לוֹ, הוּא הַמְּטַיֵּל בֵּין הַשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים.
verses.english: Having earned a few moments of privacy, she beckons to her beloved. He presents her with a bouquet of fine lilies, whereupon she contentedly exclaims:My beloved is mine, and I am his —He who pastures among the fragrant lilies.

verses.hebrew: עַד שֶׁתִּשְׁקַע הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְיִסְתַּלְּקוּ הַצְּלָלִים הָאֲרֻכִּים, טַיֵּל לְךָ אֲהוּבִי כְּמוֹ צְבִי אוֹ כְּמוֹ עוֹפֶר בֶּן אַיָּלָה, עַד הֶהָרִים הָרְחוֹקִים.
verses.english: We can delight in each other's companyUntil the peak of the day's heatWhen the shadows shall fleeAnd my entourage returns from their foxhunt.Then you must turn on your heels;Make yourself once moreLike a gazelle or a young hartOn the towering fragrant mountains.Just as they retrace their steps from time to time,You too must come and visit me.

verses.hebrew: עַל מִטָּתִי בַּלֵּילוֹת הִשְׁתּוֹקַקְתִּי אֶל זֶה שֶׁנַּפְשִׁי אוֹהֶבֶת, חִפַּשְׁתִּי אוֹתוֹ וְלֹא מָצָאתִי.
verses.english: Song 3The country girl, lying alone at night, recounts:On my bed at nightI sought the man whom my soul loves;I sought him but did not find him.I was filled with an overwhelming longingTo reunite with him.

verses.hebrew: קַמְתִּי וְהִסְתּוֹבַבְתִּי בָּעִיר בַּשְּׁוָקִים וּבָרְחוֹבוֹת, חִפַּשְׁתִּי אֶת אוֹתוֹ שֶׁנַּפְשִׁי אוֹהֶבֶת, חִפַּשְׁתִּי אוֹתוֹ וְלֹא מָצָאתִי.
verses.english: I said to myself:"Let me arise and roam the city square,The market places,The streets —I will seek him whom my soul loves." I sought him but did not find him.

verses.hebrew: מָצְאוּ אוֹתִי הַשּׁוֹמְרִים שֶׁמִּסְתּוֹבְבִים בָּעִיר –הַאִם רְאִיתֶם אֶת זֶה שֶׁנַּפְשִׁי אוֹהֶבֶת?
verses.english: My search drew meTo the outer environs of the city.There I crossed paths with the sentriesWho circle the city's periphery.I asked them:Have you seen the man whom my soul loves?

verses.hebrew: כִּמְעַט שֶׁהִצְלַחְתִּי לַעֲבוֹר מֵהֶם וְהָיִיתִי מוֹצֵאת אֶת זֶה שֶׁנַּפְשִׁי אוֹהֶבֶת, הָיִיתִי אוֹחֶזֶת בּוֹ בְּלִי לְהַרְפּוֹת עַד שֶׁהָיִיתִי מְבִיאָה אוֹתוֹ אֶל בֵּית אִמִּי – אֶל הַחֶדֶר שֶׁל הוֹרָתִי.
verses.english: When I found the man whom my soul loves.I grabbed onto him —This time I shall not let go of him.I shall bring him to my mother's house,To the room of she who conceived me —To have him permanently nearby.

verses.hebrew: מַשְׁבִּיעָה אֲנִי אֶתְכֶם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּצְּבָיִים אוֹ בָּאַיָּלוֹת שֶׁבַּשָּׂדֶה, אַל תָּעִירוּ וְאַל תְּעוֹרְרוּ אֶת הָאַהֲבָה עַד שֶׁתַּחְפּוֹץ לְהִתְעוֹרֵר מֵעַצְמָהּ.
verses.english: But once again the court women of Jerusalem were hot on her trail.She turns in their direction and exclaims:I bind you under oath,O daughters of Jerusalem —Let the gazelles and does be witness:Neither douse nor arouse our love!Let me be;Allow my desire to be realized.

verses.hebrew: רְאוּ אֶת אֲהוּבָתִי! – מִי זֹאת שֶׁעָלְתָה מִמִּדְבַּר סִינַי כְּמוֹ עָנָן עָשָׁן, מְבֻשֶּׂמֶת בְּמוֹר וּבִלְבוֹנָה וּבְכָל בּוֹשֶׂם שֶׁרוֹכְלִים מוֹכְרִים.
verses.english: Once the country girl's repeat escapade became known to the court, there was much uproar, and an enquiry began:Who is this ascending from the wilderness,Enveloped in pillars of smoke-like fragrance?Bedecked in fumes of incense —Myrrh and frankincense,All the powdery merchandise of the perfumer?

verses.hebrew: וְעַכְשָׁיו, סְבִיב מִטָּתוֹ שֶׁל הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה יֵשׁ שִׁשִּׁים גִּבּוֹרִים מִגִּבּוֹרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
verses.english: How did she escape the palace sleeping quarters?Behold! The bedroom of Shlomo —Sixty mighty warriors surround it,Of the mightiest of Israel!

verses.hebrew: כֻּלָּם מְתֻרְגָּלִים לֶאֱחוֹז בַּחֶרֶב בַּקְּרָב, כָּל אֶחָד חַרְבּוֹ עַל מוֹתְנָיו, שׁוֹמְרִים מִפַּחַד בַּלֵּילוֹת.
verses.english: All of them sword-bearing,All with combat experience!Yet each one's sword was frozen by his loins —Stricken with overwhelming fearOn those nights.

verses.hebrew: הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה עָשָׂה לְעַצְמוֹ אַפִּרְיוֹן מְפוֹאָר לְמִטָּתוֹ מֵעֲצֵי הַלְּבָנוֹן.
verses.english: And how did she escape under the noses of her fellow courtiers?King Shlomo had singled her outFor marriage as a premier wife!King Shlomo had crafted a magnificent bridal canopyFor the country girl and himself —He made it of Levanon wood.

verses.hebrew: אֶת עַמּוּדָיו עָשָׂה מִכֶּסֶף, אֶת הָרִצּוּף מִזָּהָב, עָלָיו פָּרוֹכֶת צֶמֶר צָבוּעַ בְּאַרְגָּמָן, תּוֹכוֹ מָלֵא אַהֲבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
verses.english: Its pillars of silver,Its beds of gold,Its curtains of purple wool.Its interior infusedWith passionate flaming love —More intense than the combined love felt towardsAll the other court girls of Jerusalem.

verses.hebrew: צְאוּ וְהַבִּיטוּ בְּנוֹת צִיּוֹן בַּמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה, בַּכֶּתֶר שֶׁאִמּוֹ עִטְּרָה אוֹתוֹ בּוֹ בְּיוֹם חֲתֻנָּתוֹ – בְּיוֹם שִׂמְחַת לִבּוֹ.
verses.english: And while dwelling in the canopy in the lead-up to her wedding, she would encourage her upgraded entourage — now comprised of the elite "girls of Zion" — to feast their eyes on the ostentatious wedding preparations:"Girls of Zion —Go and take a look at the gorgeous crownWith which King Shlomo's mother crowned himOn his wedding day,On the day his heart delighted."

verses.hebrew: אַתְּ יָפָה רַעְיָתִי, אַתְּ יָפָה – עֵינַיִךְ מִבַּעַד לְצַמָּתֵךְ יָפוֹת כְּמוֹ יוֹנִים, שַׂעְרֵךְ דּוֹמֶה לְעֵדֶר עִזִּים שֶׁגּוֹלְשׁוֹת מֵהַר הַגִּלְעָד.
verses.english: Once they were distracted, she would slink away to meet her beloved. And their love was most passionate. The shepherd boy, infatuated with her from head to toe, softly praises her:Behold you are beautiful my soulmate —You are so beautiful.Your eyes shine forth as faithful as dovesFrom beneath your kerchief;Your hair with its myriad shades —Like a flock of goatsDescending from Mount Gilad.

verses.hebrew: שִׁנַּיִךְ דּוֹמוֹת לְעֵדֶר עִזִּים זֵהוֹת שֶׁעָלוּ מִן הָרַחְצָה, כֻּלָּם תּוֹאֲמוֹת וְאֵין בָּהֶם פְּגָם.
verses.english: Your teeth — so uniform, such a pristine white —Like a flock of identical sheepJust now ascended from their wash;All harmonious,No blemish among them.

verses.hebrew: שִׂפְתוֹתַיִךְ כְּחוּט אָדוֹם בּוֹהֵק, וְדִבּוּרֵךְ נָאֶה, רַקָּתֵךְ מִבַּעַד לְצַמָּתֵךְ כְּפֶלַח רִמּוֹן.
verses.english: Your lips — a deep red —Like a scarlet thread;Your speech so fair.Wrapped within your kerchief,You are filled with inner beauty of character —Like a slice of luscious pomegranate.

verses.hebrew: צַוָּארֵךְ מְקֻשָּׁט כְּמִגְדַּל דָּוִד שֶׁבָּנוּי לְמוֹפֵת, תְּלוּיִים עָלָיו אֶלֶף מְגִנִּים וְכָל נַרְתִּיקֵי חִצֵּי הַגִּבּוֹרִים.
verses.english: Your neck is like the Tower of Dovid,Built as a military fortress;A thousand shields hang upon it,With all the quivers of the mighty.

verses.hebrew: שְׁנֵי שָׁדַיִךְ כִּשְׁנֵי עוֹפָרִים תְּאוֹמִים בְּנֵי צְבִיָּה שֶׁרוֹעִים בֵּין הַשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים.
verses.english: Your two breasts — desirous twins —Like two fawnsPasturing among the fragrant lilies.

verses.hebrew: עַד שֶׁתִּשְׁקַע הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְיִסְתַּלְּקוּ הַצְּלָלִים הָאֲרֻכִּים, אֲטַיֵּל לִי אִתָּךְ אֶל הַר בּוֹשֶׂם הַמּוֹר – אֶל גִּבְעַת הַלְּבוֹנָה.
verses.english: Let us delight in each other's companyUntil the peak of the day's heatWhen the shadows fleeAnd your entourage returns from its forages —Then I must be offTo the mountain of myrrhAnd the hill of frankincense.

verses.hebrew: כֻּלָּךְ יָפָה רַעְיָתִי, אֵין בָּךְ שׁוּם פְּגָם.
verses.english: But how can I leave youWhen everything about you is fair, my soulmate,And you are without blemish!?

verses.hebrew: יַחַד אִתִּי מֵהַלְּבָנוֹן כַּלָּתִי, בּוֹאִי יַחַד אִתִּי מֵהַלְּבָנוֹן, הַבִּיטִי מֵרֹאשׁ הָרֵי אֲמָנָה, מֵרֹאשׁ פִּסְגַת הַחֶרְמוֹן הַמֻּשְׁלֶגֶת, מִמְּעוֹנוֹת הָאֲרָיוֹת מֵהַָרֵי הַנְּמֵרִים.
verses.english: I shall arrange for you to come with me —I shall take you as my bride;With me you will come from the Levanon canopy.You will look back at your captivityFrom the peaks of Amanah, Snir and Chermon,Where none shall dare pursue youFor fear of the lions' densAnd the mountains of leopards.

verses.hebrew: כָּבַשְׁתְּ אֶת לִבִּי אֲחוֹתִי כַּלָּתִי, כָּבַשְׁתְּ אֶת לִבִּי כְּבָר בְּאַחַת מֵעֵינַיִךְ, בְּאַחַת מִשַּׁרְשְׁרוֹת צַוָּארֵךְ.
verses.english: You bound my heart to yours,My equal — my sister.You bound my heart to yoursWith but one of your eyes,With but a single pendant of your necklace.Although one of your eyes is ever watchful,On the look-out for those who pursue you,And although I get to enjoy so little of youSince King Shlomo has proclaimed you his —You have still captivated my heart.

verses.hebrew: מַה יָּפָה אַהֲבָתֵךְ אֲחוֹתִי כַּלָּתִי, כֹּה טוֹבָה אַהֲבָתֵךְ יוֹתֵר מִיַּיִן וְרֵיחַ הַשֶּׁמֶן שֶׁלָּךְ מְבֻשָּׂם יוֹתֵר מִכָּל הַבְּשָׂמִים.
verses.english: How fair is your love, my sister and bride;How your love surpasses wine for rousing my spirit,And the fragrance of your perfumed oils —All spices.

verses.hebrew: שִׂפְתוֹתַיִךְ נוֹטְפוֹת מְתִיקוּת כַּלָּתִי, דְּבַשׁ וְחָלָב שׁוֹפְעִים מִלְּשׁוֹנֵךְ, וְרֵיחַ שִׂמְלוֹתַיִךְ כְּרֵיחַ הַלְּבָנוֹן.
verses.english: The lovers draw close and passionately kiss. The shepherd boy remarks:Your lips, my bride, are dripping with sweetness —The honey and milkBeneath your tongue;The scent of your garmentsSmelling like the royal Levanon canopy.

verses.hebrew: אֲחוֹתִי כַּלָּתִי הִיא כְּמוֹ גַּן נָעוּל, מְקוֹר מַיִם נָעוּל – מַעְיָן שָׁמוּר.
verses.english: My sister and bride has saved herself for me;She is to other men like a lush garden that is locked,Its waters secured,Its spring fastened.

verses.hebrew: נְטִיעוֹתַיִךְ פַּרְדֵּס רִמּוֹנִים עִם פֵּירוֹת מְתוּקִים, וּבְשָׂמִים שֶׁל כּוֹפֶר וְנֵרְדְּ.
verses.english: Your vegetation — delicious —A pomegranate orchard with luscious fruits;Fragrant with henna scents and spikenard scents —

verses.hebrew: נֵרְדְּ וְכַרְכּוֹם קָנֶה וְקִנָּמוֹן וְכָל עֲצֵי לְבוֹנָה, מוֹר וַאֲהָל וְכָל שׁוֹרְשֵׁי בְּשָׂמִים.
verses.english: Spikenard and saffron,Calamus and cinnamon,All the frankincense trees,Myrrh and aloes —All the major spices.

verses.hebrew: מֻשְׁקִים בְּמַעְיַן שֶׁל גַּנִּים, בְּאֵר מַיִם חַיִּים, וְנוֹזְלִים מֵהַלְּבָנוֹן.
verses.english: The spring of your garden —A well of life-giving watersThat flow forth from the royal Levanon canopy.

verses.hebrew: הִתְעוֹרְרִי רוּחַ צָפוֹן וּבוֹאִי רוּחַ דָּרוֹם, נַשְּׁבִי בְּגַנִּי וְיַשְׁקֶה הַגֶּשֶׁם אֶת בְּשָׂמָיו, וְאָז יָבוֹא אֲהוּבִי לְגַנּוֹ וְיֹאכַל מִפֵּרוֹתָיו הַמְּתוּקִים.
verses.english: The country girl responds:Awaken, o' wind of the north!Come, o' wind of the south!Blow upon my garden —Give off its fragrances!Let my beloved come to his gardenAnd feast on its luscious fruit!

verses.hebrew: בָּאתִי לְגַנִּי אֲחוֹתִי הַכַּלָּה, לִקַּטְתִּי מוֹר וּשְׁאָר בּוֹשֶׂם, אָכַלְתִּי מִקְּנֵה הַסֻּכָּר וּמְתִיקוּתוֹ הַנִּשְׁפֶּכֶת, שָׁתִיתִי מֵהַיַּיִן הָאָדוֹם וְהַלָּבָן, אִכְלוּ יְדִידִים שְׁתוּ וְשִׁכְרוּ אֲהוּבִים.
verses.english: The shepherd boy makes love and romantically sings:I have come to my garden, my sister and bride!I have gathered my myrrh with my spice,Eaten my sugar cane with my honey,Drunk my wine with my milk!Now let us celebrate —Let our friends eat,Our loved ones drinkAnd become intoxicated!

verses.hebrew: – אֲנִי יְשֵׁנָה אַךְ לִבִּי עֵר, וְהִנֵּה קוֹל אֲהוּבִי דּוֹפֵק בַּפֶּתַח: פִּתְחִי לִי אֲחוֹתִי רַעְיָתִי יוֹנָתִי תַּמָּתִי! רֹאשִׁי כְּבָר מָלֵא בְּטַל, תַּלְתַּלַּי נוֹטְפוֹת טִפּוֹת לַיְלָה!
verses.english: Song 4But their love would not continue undisturbed. The country girl was tracked down once more and forcibly returned to the palace. Placed under permanent watch, the memory of her beloved gradually faded, and she slipped into court routine.The country girl recounts:I was sleeping soundlyAlthough my heart remained somewhat awake to my lover.Then I heard the sound of my lover knocking at my door:Open up for me,My sister, my soulmate,My faithful dove, my perfect one —My head is saturated with dew,My locks with the droplets of night.

verses.hebrew: – כְּבָר פָּשַׁטְתִּי אֶת הַכֻּתּוֹנֶת אֵיךְ אֶלְבַּשׁ אוֹתָהּ? כְּבָר רָחַצְתִּי אֶת רַגְלַי אֵיךְ אֲטַנֵּף אוֹתָם?
verses.english: I replied:I have already removed my robe for the night —How can I put it back on?I have already washed my feet —How can I soil them once more?

verses.hebrew: אֲהוּבִי סִלֵּק אֶת יָדוֹ מֵחוֹר הַמַּנְעוּל לְהִסְתַּלֵּק, וּמִיַּד הִתְגַּעְגַּעְתִּי אֵלָיו.
verses.english: But my beloved sent forth his hand from the portalTo try and unlock the door himself,And my innards trembled for himBy my hitherto suppressed feelings towards him.

verses.hebrew: מִיַּד קַמְתִּי לִפְתּוֹחַ לַאֲהוּבִי וְעַל יָדַי וְאֶצְבְּעוֹתַי לִקְרָאתוֹ בּוֹשֶׂם מוֹר שֶׁנָּטַף עַל יָדִית הַמַּנְעוּל.
verses.english: I arose to open the door for my beloved;My hands coursed with passion —As though dripping with myrrh,My fingers imbibed with the scent of myrrh —So long as they were hovering above the lock.Yet each time I touched it,The passion vanished into thin airAnd I hesitated.

verses.hebrew: פָּתַחְתִּי לַאֲהוּבִי אַךְ אֲהוּבִי כְּבָר חָמַק וְעָבַר, נַפְשִׁי יָצְאָה כְּשֶׁאָמַר שֶׁהוּא עוֹזֵב, חִפַּשְׂתִּי אוֹתוֹ וְלֹא מָצָאתִי, קָרָאתִי וְהוּא לֹא עָנָה לִי.
verses.english: Eventually I opened the door,But my beloved had stolen away —Stung by my ambivalence.My life was knocked out of meBy his harsh departing words.I searched for him but did not find him;I called out to him but he did not answer.

verses.hebrew: מָצְאוּ אוֹתִי הַשּׁוֹמְרִים שֶׁמִּסְתּוֹבְבִים בָּעִיר הִכּוּ וּפָצְעוּ אוֹתִי, שׁוֹמְרֵי הַחוֹמוֹת לָקְחוּ אֶת צְעִיפִי מֵעָלַי.
verses.english: As my frantic search led me towards the countryside,I crossed paths with the sentriesWho circle the city's periphery.They hit me and injured me;They stripped me of my adornments —Those guards of the walls.

verses.hebrew: מַשְׁבִּיעָה אֲנִי אֶתְכֶם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, אִם תִּמְצְאוּ אֶת אֲהוּבִי מַה תַּגִּידוּ לוֹ? – שֶׁאֲנִי חוֹלַת אַהֲבָה!
verses.english: Exasperated and defeated, she turns to her entourage:I bind you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem:If you find my beloved —What shall you tell him?That I am lovesick for him.

verses.hebrew: – מַה מְּיוּחָד בַּאֲהוּבֵךְ מִשְּׁאָר הָאֲהוּבִים, הַיָּפָה בַּנָּשִׁים? מַה מְּיוּחָד בַּאֲהוּבֵךְ מִשְּׁאָר הָאֲהוּבִים שֶׁכָּכָה אַתְּ מַשְׁבִּיעָה אוֹתָנוּ?
verses.english: Surprised by the intensity of her love, her entourage asks:How does your love differ from other loves,O' fairest among women?What makes your lover differ from other lovers —That you have imposed this oath upon us?

verses.hebrew: – אֲהוּבִי בָּהִיר וּפָנָיו וְרֻדּוֹת, אֵין אֶחָד מֵרְבָבָה כָּמוֹהוּ.
verses.english: The country girl responds, her voice now radiant:The complexion of my beloved —As fair as pure white,As ruddy as red;He stands out from the myriads.

verses.hebrew: רֹאשׁוֹ אוֹצַר זָהָב, שְׂעָרוֹתָיו תַּלְתַּלִּים שְׁחוֹרוֹת כְּעוֹרֵב.
verses.english: His head — as thoughPlated with a sheet of exquisite gemstone;His layered ringlets as black as a raven.

verses.hebrew: עֵינָיו כְּמוֹ יוֹנִים עַל מַעְיְנוֹת מַיִם, רוֹחֲצוֹת בְּחָלָב, מְמֻקָּמוֹת בִּשְׁלֵמוּת.
verses.english: His eyes gaze at meLike a dove at a creek's torrent;A pristine white as though bathed in milk,Perfectly set in their sockets.

verses.hebrew: לְחָיָיו כַּעֲרוּגַת בּוֹשֶׂם שֶׁגְּדֵלִים בָּהּ תַּמְרוּקִים, שִׂפְתוֹתָיו כְּמוֹ שׁוֹשַׁנִּים שֶׁנּוֹטְפוֹת מִבּוֹשֶׂם הַמּוֹר.
verses.english: His cheeks — chiselledLike the furrows of a spice patchIn which perfumes are cultivated.His lips like lily blossoms,Dripping with wafting myrrh.

verses.hebrew: יָדָיו כְּמוֹ מְגִלּוֹת שֶׁל זָהָב מְמֻלָּאוֹת בְּאַבְנֵי תַּרְשִׁישׁ, מֵעָיו כְּמוֹ שֶׁנְהָב מְכֻסֶּה בְּאַבְנֵי סַפִּיר.
verses.english: His arms — like golden cylindersFilled with gems of Tarsus;His stomach — as thoughPlated with ivory sheets,Translucent like sapphires.

verses.hebrew: שׁוֹקָיו כְּמוֹ עַמּוּדֵי שַׁיִשׁ עַל יְסוֹדוֹת אַדְנֵי זָהָב, מַרְאֵהוּ כְּאֶרֶז מֻבְחָר בַּלְּבָנוֹן.
verses.english: His legs — like marble pillarsSet in sockets of exquisite gemstone.His appearance — as beautifulAs the royal Levanon canopy;As strong as its cedars.

verses.hebrew: דִּבְרֵי פִּיו מַמְתַּקִּים, וְכֻלּוֹ מַחֲמַדִּים, זֶה אֲהוּבִי וְזֶה יְדִידִי, בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
verses.english: His palate exudes sweet delights;Everything about him is desirable.This is my beloved,This is my soul mate,O daughters of Jerusalem.

verses.hebrew: – לְאָן הָלַךְ אֲהוּבֵךְ, הַיָּפָה בַּנָּשִׁים? לְאָן פָּנָה אֲהוּבֵךְ וּנְחַפֵּשׂ אוֹתוֹ אִתָּךְ?
verses.english: Song 5Deeply impressed by her descriptions, the entourage resolves to no longer harass the country girl; from now on they will help in her quest to reunite with him.The entourage asks:Where has your beloved gone,O fairest among women?In which direction did your beloved head?We shall seek him with you.

verses.hebrew: – אֲהוּבִי יָרַד לְגַנּוֹ לַעֲרוּגוֹת הַבְּשָׂמִים, לְטַיֵּיל בַּגַּנִּים וּלְלַקֵּט שׁוֹשַׁנִּים.
verses.english: Just then, the country girl looks up and sees her lover approaching from a distance.She calls out:My beloved has descended from the mountains,Headed towards his garden —Towards me, his prized spice patch.He is coming to tend to the garden,To gather his sweet-scented lilies — my love.

verses.hebrew: אֲנִי מְיוֹעֶדֶת לַאֲהוּבִי וַאֲהוּבִי מְיוֹעָד לִי, הוּא הַמְּטַיֵּל בֵּין הַשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים.
verses.english: I am my beloved's and my beloved is mine —He who tends to the lilies.

verses.hebrew: רַעְיָתִי, אַתְּ יָפָה כְּעִיר הַבִּירָה, נָאָה כִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, חֲזָקָה כִּצְבָא גְּדוּדִים.
verses.english: The shepherd boy arrives and beholds his beautiful bride once more:You are so fair my soulmate,Now that we have made upAnd desire one another once more.As splendid as all the girls of Jerusalem —Now awesome and untouchable,As though surrounded by military formations!

verses.hebrew: הַפְנִי אֵלַי אֶת מַבָּטֵךְ הוּא מְרוֹמֵם אוֹתִי, שַׂעְרֵךְ דּוֹמֶה לְעֵדֶר עִזִּים שֶׁגּוֹלְשׁוֹת מֵהַגִּלְעָד.
verses.english: Turn your eyes from my opponent —From cautiously looking out for King Shlomo —Gaze only at me,For they make me proud.Your hair with its myriad highlights —Like a flock of goatsDescending from Mount Gilad.

verses.hebrew: שִׁנַּיִךְ דּוֹמוֹת לְעֵדֶר כְּבָשִׂים שֶׁעָלוּ מִן הָרַחְצָה, כֻּלָּם תּוֹאֲמוֹת וְאֵין בָּהֶם פְּגָם.
verses.english: Your teeth — so uniform, such a pristine white —Like a flock of identical sheepAscended from their wash;All harmonious,No blemish among them.

verses.hebrew: רַקָּתֵךְ מִבַּעַד לְצַמָּתֵךְ דּוֹמָה לְפֶלַח רִמּוֹן.
verses.english: Like a slice of luscious pomegranate,Filled with inner beauty of character,Wrapped within your kerchief.

verses.hebrew: שִׁשִּׁים מַלְכּוֹת יֵשׁ לִי וּשְׁמוֹנִים פִּילַגְשִׁים וַעֲלָמוֹת לְלֹא מִסְפָּר.
verses.english: He turns to her entourage and defiantly asks:Are there not sixty queens,Eighty concubines,Countless young women at the king's service?

verses.hebrew: אַךְ יוֹנָתִי הַמֻּשְׁלֶמֶת הִיא יְחִידָה, הִיא יְחִידָה וּמְיוּחֶדֶת לָאֵם שֶׁיָּלְדָה אוֹתָהּ, כָּל הַבָּנוֹת רָאוּ אוֹתָהּ וְאִשְּׁרוּ, וְהַמְּלָכוֹת וְהַפִּילַגְשִׁים הִלְלוּ אוֹתָהּ.
verses.english: Yet he demands to possess my one faithful dove,My one and only love!Unique among her mother's offspring!She who combines the choicest elements of beautyFor the woman who bore her!All the girls who behold her approve of her;All the queens and concubines praise her!

verses.hebrew: מִי זֹאת שֶׁנִּרְאֵית כְּמוֹ הַשַּׁחַר, יָפָה כַּלְּבָנָה מְיוּחֶדֶת כַּחַמָּה, חֲזָקָה כִּצְבָא גְּדוּדִים!
verses.english: The girls of the entourage approach the country girl: Who is this who has come to gaze down,Radiant like the breaking dawn?Fair as the setting moon,Clear as the rising sun,Awesome as the star formations?

verses.hebrew: יָרַדְתִּי אֶל גִּנַּת אֱגוֹז לִרְאוֹת אֶת אֲבִיב פֵּרוֹת הַנַּחַל, לִרְאוֹת הַאִם הַגֶּפֶן פָּרְחָה, אִם צָמְחוּ נִצָּנֵי הָרִמּוֹנִים.
verses.english: The country girl replies:Consciously, I was simply descending to the garden of nuts,To behold the vegetation lining the brooks —To see whether the vines had blossomed,Whether the pomegranates had bloomed.

verses.hebrew: – לֹא יָדַעְתִּי מִכָּךְ, הָיִיתִי חָפֵצָה לִהְיוֹת בְּמֶרְכְּבוֹת עַמִּי הָאוֹהֵב!
verses.english: I was not aware that subconsciouslyThe love of my soul had mobilized me like a chariot,Transporting me from the palaceBack to my laypeople.

verses.hebrew: – שׁוּבִי שׁוּבִי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם הַבְּנוּיָה, שׁוּבִי שׁוּבִי וְנַבִּיט בָּךְ, מַה תַּבִּיטוּ בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם הַבְּנוּיָה בְּהִתְכַּנְּסוּת הַמַּחֲנוֹת!
verses.english: Realizing she is set on leaving the palace never to return, her entourage implores her to stay:Do come back, O come back, counterpart of Shlomo!Do come back, O come back —We will look up to you.But the country girl rejects them:How can you look up to the counterpart of ShlomoWhen she is a prisoner,Encircled by two encampments?

verses.hebrew: מַה יָּפוּ צְעָדַיִךְ בָּעֲלִיָּה לָרֶגֶל, בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל הָאֵל הַמֵּטִיב, סִתְרֵי יְרֵכַיִךְ דּוֹמִים לְתַכְשִׁיטִים מַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵי אָמָּן.
verses.english: Her entourage tries another approach:How fair are your feet, O daughter of nobility,So long as they rest in the fine shoesGifted to you by Shlomo —Out in the country they will blister and crack.That which your thighs conceal are like jewelsSo long as they are fashioned by a craftsman.Your extreme feminine beautyIs contingent on maintenance and careThat only the palace can provide.

verses.hebrew: טַבּוּרֵךְ כַּאֲגַרְטָל בְּצוּרַת סַהַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ חָסֵר יַיִן לִמְזִיגָה, בִּטְנֵךְ כַּעֲרֵמַת חִטִּים מֻקֶּפֶת שׁוֹשַׁנִּים.
verses.english: Your navel — like a moonlit poolNever lacking mixed wine;Your stomach — like a heap of wheatSo long as you are hedged with lilies —The luxury and bounty of the palace.

verses.hebrew: שְׁנֵי שָׁדַיִךְ כִּשְׁנֵי עוֹפָרִים תְּאוֹמִים בְּנֵי צְבִיָּה.
verses.english: Your two breasts — desirous twins,Like two fawns;

verses.hebrew: צַוָּארֵךְ כְּמִגְדַּל שֶׁנְהָב, עֵינַיִךְ צְלוּלוֹת כִּבְרֵכוֹת הַמַּיִם שֶׁעַל יַד הַשַּׁעַר הָרָאשִׁי שֶׁל הָעִיר חֶשְׁבּוֹן, אַפֵּךְ כַּמִּגְדַּל בִּלְבָנוֹן שֶׁצּוֹפֶה לְעֵבֶר דַּמֶּשֶׂק.
verses.english: Your neck — like an ivory tower;Your eyes shimmerLike the pools of Heshbon —Worthy of a city gate frequented by the multitudes,But wasted on villagersWho cannot appreciate your beauty.Your nose — perfectly straight,Like the Tower of LebanonOverlooking the environs of Damascus.

verses.hebrew: רֹאשֵׁךְ שֶׁעָלַיִךְ דּוֹמֶה לְהַר הַכַּרְמֶל, וְצַמּוֹתַיִךְ הַתְּלוּיוֹת כְּחוּטֵי אַרְגָּמָן, הַמֶּלֶךְ קָשׁוּר בְּאַהֲבָה בְּשַׂעֲרוֹתַיִךְ הַגּוֹלְשׁוֹת.
verses.english: Your head sits atop your bodyWith a majesty akin to the Carmel crags;Your hair sways around your headFine as royal purple —The king has is love bound in its locks.

verses.hebrew: כֹּה יָפָה וְכֹה נְעִימָה אַתְּ, אַהֲבָה עֲנֻגָּה.
verses.english: Her entourage turns and philosophically addresses love:How fair and pleasant you are, O love —When complimented by sensual delights.

verses.hebrew: קוֹמָתֵךְ הַזְּקוּפָה דּוֹמָה לְעֵץ תָּמָר וְשָׁדַיִךְ לְאֶשְׁכּוֹלוֹת הַתְּמָרִים.
verses.english: Now King Shlomo himself appears and attempts to win back the heart of his beautiful fiancée:This posture of yours is like a palm tree —So magnificent and tall;Your breasts hang so highLike its date clusters.

verses.hebrew: אָמַרְתִּי, אֶעֱלֶה עַל עֵץ הַתָּמָר, אוֹחַז בַּעֲנָפָיו, וְיִהְיוּ עַכְשָׁיו שָׁדַיִךְ כְּאֶשְׁכְּלוֹת עֲנָבִים, וְרֵיחַ נְשִׁימָתֵךְ כְּרֵיחַ תַּפּוּחִים.
verses.english: I said to myself:I must climb this palm tree —Its trunk is tall and smoothBut I shall clutch its bark protrusions.I beg you —Should I successfully climb to your heart —May your breasts be to meLike the clusters of the vine;The scent of your breathWafts from your nose like fragrant apples —

verses.hebrew: וְטַעֲמֵךְ כְּיַיִן טוֹב עֲבוּר אַהֲבָה אֲמִתִּית, שֶׁגּוֹרֵם גַּם לִישֵׁנִים לְשׂוֹחֵחַ.
verses.english: Your palate like delightful fine wine…But the country girl defiantly cuts him off:No — it shall go to my beloved,To he who embodies honesty,To he who makes my sleeping lips murmur:

verses.hebrew: – אֲנִי מְיוֹעֶדֶת לַאֲהוּבִי וּתְשׁוּקָתוֹ הִיא בִּי.
verses.english: I am my beloved's,And his desire is upon me.

verses.hebrew: בֹּא אֲהוּבִי נֵצֵא לַשָּׂדֶה, נָלוּן בֵּין בִּשְׂמֵי הַכֹּפֶר.
verses.english: She turns to her lover:Come, my beloved —Let us head out to the fields,Spend the night in the villagesSurrounding Jerusalem.

verses.hebrew: נָקוּם הַשְׁכֵּם בַּבּוֹקֶר וְנֵצֵא לַכְּרָמִים, נִרְאֶה אִם פָּרְחוּ פִּרְחֵי הַגֶּפֶן, אִם נִפְתְּחוּ עִנְבֵי הַסְּמָדַר הַזְּעִירִים, אִם צָמְחוּ נִצָּנֵי הָרִמּוֹנִים, שָׁם אַעֲנִיק לְךָ אֶת אַהֲבָתִי.
verses.english: Let us rise early for the vineyards;See if the vine has blossomed,If the tender grapes have emerged,If the pomegranates are in bloom.Regardless of their condition —My love for you has ripened;There I shall give you my love.

verses.hebrew: פִּרְחֵי הַיַּסְמִין הִדִּיפוּ רֵיחַ, לְפִתְחֵנוּ מְצוּיִים כָּל מִינֵי פֵּרוֹת מְתוּקִים טְרִיִּים וִיבֵשִׁים, שָׁמַרְתִּי לְךָ מֵהֶם, אֲהוּבִי!
verses.english: The mandrakes yield their fragrance for everyone;Outside our doors grow all delectable fruits.They may be fresh but feel old —Dulled by abundance and habituation.But my love for you is fresh and untainted;I have hidden it solely for you.

verses.hebrew: מִי יִתֵּן שֶׁתִּהְיֶה כְּאָחִי שֶׁיָּנַק מֵהַשָּׁדַיִם שֶׁל אִמִּי, וּכְשֶׁאֶפְגּוֹשׁ אוֹתְךָ בַּחוּץ אֲנַשֵּׁק אוֹתְךָ וְלֹא יָבוּזוּ לִי.
verses.english: Thus the country girl and her beloved leave the palace for good, and head off for life together in the fields. But while deeply in love with the shepherd, she begins to pine for the creature comforts of her former palace life. She shares her fantasy with her beloved:If only you could have been an equal to me —As though you were my brother,Nursed by my mother's breasts.If only you had been a member of the royal family,Receiving the same 'maternal' care I did —Then I could kiss youWhen encountering you out in the open,And no one would scorn me.

verses.hebrew: וְאוֹבִיל וַאֲבִיא אוֹתְךָ לְבֵית אִמִּי כְּהֶרְגְּלֵנוּ, וְאֶמְזוֹג לְךָ מֵהַיַּיִן הַמְּבֻשָּׂם וּמִמִּיץ הָרִמּוֹן.
verses.english: I could lead you,Bring you into my 'maternal' home —You could teach me.I could offer you spiced wineAnd my pomegranate nectar.

verses.hebrew: יַד שְׂמֹאלוֹ שֶׁל אֲהוּבִי תִּתְמוֹךְ בְּרֹאשִׁי וְיַד יְמִינוֹ תְּחַבֵּק אוֹתִי.
verses.english: She snaps back to the passionate love of her present reality, and airs her thoughts as though addressing her former entourage:But now he unabashedly makes love with me;He places his left hand under my head,Embraces me with his right arm.

verses.hebrew: מַשְׁבִּיעָה אֲנִי אֶתְכֶם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, אַל תָּעִירוּ וְאַל תְּעוֹרְרוּ אֶת הָאַהֲבָה עַד שֶׁתַּחְפּוֹץ לְהִתְעוֹרֵר מֵעַצְמָה.
verses.english: Need I bind you under oath,Daughters of Jerusalem!?How could you douse or arouse our love,Interfere with my desire being actualized!?You no longer have any power over me.

verses.hebrew: רְאוּ אֶת אֲהוּבָתִי – מִי זֹאת שֶׁעָלְתָה מִמִּדְבַּר סִינַי מִתְרַפֶּקֶת עַל אֲהוּבָהּ! תַּחַת עֵץ הַתַּפּוּחַ עוֹרַרְתִּי אֶת אַהֲבָתְךָ עַם יִשְׂרָאֵל, שָׁמָּה הָיוּ חֶבְלֵי הַלֵּדָה שֶׁל אִמְּךָ, שָׁמָּה יָלְדָה אוֹתְךָ.
verses.english: The narrator questions:Who is this palace maidenWho rises from the wildernessYet holds her beloved so close?The shepherd boy responds:No — in her essence,She is a fellow countrywoman.Beneath the apple tree I first aroused you;There your mother's womb contracted with you;There she who bore youCaused her own mother's womb to contract.

verses.hebrew: שִׂים אוֹתִי כְּטַבַּעַת עַל לִבְּךָ – כְּטַבַּעַת עַל זְרוֹעֲךָ, כִּי הָאַהֲבָה עַזָּה כַּמָּוֶת – קִנְאָתְךָ לִי קָשָׁה כְּמוֹ הַשְּׁאוֹל, לוֹהֶטֶת כְּשַׁלְהֶבֶת אֵשׁ.
verses.english: The country girl turns once more to her lover:Set me like a seal upon your heart,A seal upon your arm —May you always cherish meAnd protect me from the desirous king.For although our love is as intense as death,The king's jealousy is as harsh as the grave.But ultimately our love shall triumph —Its blaze is ablazeWith roaring flames.

verses.hebrew: גַּם מַיִם רַבִּים לֹא יוּכְלוּ לְכַבּוֹת אֶת הָאַהֲבָה – נְהָרוֹת לֹא יִשְׁטְפוּ אוֹתָהּ, אִם יִתֵּן אִישׁ אֶת כָּל הוֹן בֵּיתוֹ תְּמוּרַת אַהֲבָה זוֹ, יִלְעֲגוּ לוֹ.
verses.english: The narrator reflects:Indeed, love shall ultimately triumph.Many waters cannot douse love;Raging rivers cannot sweep it away.Even if a man — as wealthy as Shlomo —Offers all the wealth of his estateTo rupture the lovers' bond,They will simply scoff at him.

verses.hebrew: אָמְרוּ עָלַי: יֵשׁ לָנוּ אָחוֹת צְעִירָה שֶׁטֶּרֶם צָמְחוּ שָׁדֶיהָ, מַה נַּעֲשֶׂה לַאֲחוֹתֵנוּ בַּיּוֹם שֶׁיְּבַקְּשׁוּ לָשֵׂאת אוֹתָהּ?
verses.english: Song 6The country girl turns to her lover, concern upon her face:We have a little sister —A fellow country girl;She is still young and has no breasts.What can we do for our sisterOn the day she is discussed in the royal court?How can we spare her my ordeal; Save her from the clutches of the king?

verses.hebrew: אִם הִיא חוֹמָה נִבְנֶה עָלֶיהָ טִירָה שֶׁל כֶּסֶף, וְאִם הִיא דֶּלֶת נַקִּיף אוֹתָהּ בְּלוּחַ אֶרֶז.
verses.english: The shepherd boy answers pragmatically:If she is as resolute as a wallIn her adamance to evade the king,We can build about her a fortress of love —Find her a suitor who will enrapture her.But if there are gaps in her defences,As though she is a door —Sometimes open to cooperation with the king —We must board her up with panels of cedar.

verses.hebrew: אֲנִי שְׁמוּרָה כְּמוֹ חוֹמָה וְשָׁדַי כְּבָר כְּמִגְדָּלִים, כָּךְ אֲנִי מֻשְׁלֶמֶת וּמוֹצֵאת חֵן בְּעֵינֵי אֲהוּבִי.
verses.english: The little country girl chimes in:I am like a wall;My breasts — as unconquerable as turrets.Therefore, in his eyes, I am viewed as oneWith whom it is worthwhileTo seek a begrudging peace.He knows I am indefatigable;He has resigned himself to never possessing me.

verses.hebrew: לַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה הָיָה כֶּרֶם בְּבִקְעַת הַכְּרָמִים, הוּא נָתַן אֶת הַכֶּרֶם לַשּׁוֹמְרִים שֶׁכָּל אִישׁ יָבִיא תְּמוּרַת פֵּרוֹתָיו אֶלֶף שִׁקְלֵי כֶּסֶף.
verses.english: Shlomo has already tried me once —He had a vineyard in the plain of multitudes,In which he cultivated endless vines.He entrusted this vineyard to caretakers;Each presented him with one thousand pieces of silverFor its vast fruit yield.

verses.hebrew: הֲשִׁיבוּ אֶת כַּרְמִי שֶׁלִּי לְפָנַי, קַח לְךָ שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת הָאֶלֶף, וְעוֹד מָאתַיִם לַשּׁוֹמְרִים אֶת פֵּרוֹתָיו!
verses.english: This became my vineyard,Which Shlomo placed entirely at my disposal.But I rejected it:The thousand silvers are yours, Shlomo —As well as the two-hundred shareFor those who took care of its fruit.

verses.hebrew: – אֲהוּבָתִי הַיּוֹשֶׁבֶת בַּגַּנִּים, חֲבֵרַי מַקְשִׁיבִים לִשְׁמוֹעַ אֶת קוֹלֵךְ, הַשְׁמִיעִי לִי אוֹתוֹ!
verses.english: The shepherd boy glances anxiously around him, deciding he had better take his leave:Listen — you who sitIn the rural suburbs of the city:Fellow people are listening in to our conversation.I must return to the safety of the wilderness —But do let me hear your voiceFrom time to time.

verses.hebrew: – בְּרַח מֵהֶם אֲהוּבִי, הֱיֵה דּוֹמֶה לִצְבִי אוֹ לְעוֹפֶר בֶּן אַיָּלָה עַל הָרֵי בְּשָׂמִים.
verses.english: She replies:Flee, beloved one —Make yourself once moreLike a gazelle or a young hartOn the fragrant spice mountains.Just as they retrace their steps from time to time —You too please come and visit me.
